chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abu Basir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The maternal uncle and the maternal aunt inherit if there is no one with them who inherits other than them.
Indeed, Allah, the Exalted, says: 'And those of kinship among each other are nearer [to one another] in the Book of Allah.'

key_terms.أَوْلى بِبَعْضٍ: Nearer to one another / more entitled

ai.seo_question: Who inherits if there are no direct descendants or parents?
ai.summary: This hadith from the Tahdhib clarifies that the maternal uncle and aunt inherit only in the absence of closer relatives, a nuance that distinguishes them from the paternal uncle who may inherit alongside others. By citing the verse on 'those of kinship' (ulu al-arham), the Imam grounds this specific ruling in the general Quranic principle of prioritizing blood ties, a key topic in Shia juristic debates regarding the exclusion of spouses or the distribution among multiple uncles.
